BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to bodygripping traps; and amending RCW 77.15.192,77.15.194, and 77.15.190.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 77.15.192 and 2001 c 1 s 2 are each amended to read asfollows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The definitions in this section apply throughout RCW ((77.15.194))77.15.190 through 77.15.198. (1) "Animal" means any nonhuman vertebrate. (2) "Bodygripping trap" means a trap that grips an animal's bodyor body part. Bodygripping trap includes, but is not limited to,steeljawed leghold traps, paddedjaw leghold traps, Conibear traps,neck snares, and nonstrangling foot snares. Cage and box traps,suitcasetype live beaver traps, and common rat and mouse traps are notconsidered bodygripping traps. (3) "Person" means a human being and, where appropriate, a publicor private corporation, an unincorporated association, a partnership,a government, or a governmental instrumentality. (4) "Raw fur" means a pelt that has not been processed for purposesof retail sale. p. 1 HB 1137 (5) "Animal problem" means any animal that threatens or damagestimber ((or)), public or private property, or threatens or injureslivestock or any other domestic animal.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 77.15.194 and 2003 c 53 s 374 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1)(a) Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, it isunlawful to use or authorize the use of any steeljawed leghold trap,neck snare, or other bodygripping trap to capture any mammal forrecreation or commerce in fur. (b) A person who has completed a course in safe, humane, and propertrapping as provided in RCW 77.65.460 may use a steeljawed legholdtrap, a neck snare, or other bodygripping traps if the trap: (i) Operates, and is operated, consistent with established,applicable furbearer trapping best management practices recognized bythe commission and either adopted by an association that representsNorth America's fish and wildlife management agencies or is otherwiseacknowledged in either academic literature or international treaties;or (ii) In the absence of scientific testing or academic literature,has been approved for use by the commission for a specific species ofmammals that are causing an animal problem or has the potential tocause an animal problem. (c) The director may grant a permit to a person to use a steeljawed leghold trap, a neck snare, or other bodygripping trap for thepurposes of protecting people from threats to their health and safety. (2) It is unlawful to knowingly buy, sell, barter, or otherwiseexchange, or offer to buy, sell, barter, or otherwise exchange the rawfur of a mammal or a mammal that has been trapped in this state ((witha steeljawed leghold trap or any other bodygripping trap, whether ornot pursuant to permit)) in violation of this section. (3) It is unlawful to use or authorize the use of any steeljawedleghold trap or any other bodygripping trap to capture any animal((,except as provided in subsections (4) and (5) of this section)) with atrap type not approved for use under subsection (1) of this section. (4) ((Nothing in this section prohibits the use of a Conibear trapin water, a padded leghold trap, or a nonstrangling type foot snarewith a special permit granted by the director under (a) through (d) of HB 1137 p. 2 this subsection. Issuance of the special permits shall be governed byrules adopted by the department and in accordance with the requirementsof this section. Every person granted a special permit to use a trapor device listed in this subsection shall check the trap or device atleast every twentyfour hours. (a) Nothing in this section prohibits the director, in consultationwith the department of social and health services or the United Statesdepartment of health and human services from granting a permit to usetraps listed in this subsection for the purpose of protecting peoplefrom threats to their health and safety. (b) Nothing in this section prohibits the director from granting aspecial permit to use traps listed in this subsection to a person whoapplies for such a permit in writing, and who establishes that thereexists on a property an animal problem that has not been and cannot bereasonably abated by the use of nonlethal control tools, including butnot limited to guard animals, electric fencing, or box and cage traps,or if such nonlethal means cannot be reasonably applied. Upon makinga finding in writing that the animal problem has not been and cannot bereasonably abated by nonlethal control tools or if the tools cannot bereasonably applied, the director may authorize the use, setting,placing, or maintenance of the traps for a period not to exceed thirtydays. (c) Nothing in this section prohibits the director from granting aspecial permit to department employees or agents to use traps listed inthis subsection where the use of the traps is the only practical meansof protecting threatened or endangered species as designated under RCW77.08.010. (d) Nothing in this section prohibits the director from issuing apermit to use traps listed in this subsection, excluding Conibeartraps, for the conduct of legitimate wildlife research. (5) Nothing in this section prohibits the United States fish andwildlife service, its employees or agents, from using a trap listed insubsection (4) of this section where the fish and wildlife servicedetermines, in consultation with the director, that the use of suchtraps is necessary to protect species listed as threatened orendangered under the federal endangered species act (16 U.S.C. Sec.1531 et seq.). p. 3 HB 1137 (6))) A person violating this section is guilty of a grossmisdemeanor.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 77.15.190 and 1999 c 258 s 9 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) A person is guilty of unlawful trapping if the person: (a) Sets out traps that are capable of taking wild animals, gameanimals, or furbearing mammals and does not possess all licenses, tags,or permits required under this title; (b) Violates any rule of the commission or director regardingseasons, bag or possession limits, closed areas including gamereserves, closed times, or any other rule governing the trapping ofwild animals; ((or)) (c) Sets out on land a leghold trap within one thousand feet of anestablished public trail or public park unless: (i) An animal problem exists that cannot be abated through othermeans; (ii) The owner or manager of the trail or park authorizes the useof the trap; and (iii) Conspicuous signs provide notice that traps are being used inthe area; (d) Sets out on land a conibear or other instant kill trap typewith a jaw spread greater than five inches unless the trap is set with: (i) At least twothirds of the trap underwater; (ii) At least fiftyfour inches above the ground; or (iii) Within an existing structure; (e) Sets out a leghold trap on land within one thousand feet of anoccupied dwelling, unless: (i) The owner or tenant of the building has given permission to usethe trap; (ii) An animal problem exists that cannot be abated through othermeans; and (iii) The owner or tenant has been notified that there are trapsset in the area; or (f) Fails to identify the owner of the traps or devices by neither: (i) Attaching a metal tag with the owner's departmentassignedidentification number or the name and address of the trapper legibly HB 1137 p. 4 written in numbers or letters not less than oneeighth inch in height;nor (ii) Inscribing into the metal of the trap such number or name andaddress. (2) Unlawful trapping is a misdemeanor.
